Messages.Author: cordovader
Messages.Body:
There are a lot of problems in your strategy:

1. How do you expect to kill?
2. What will you do after you play your first Chameleon? You're playing no Banishment.
3. How do you expect to survive bleed&stealth, vote or combat decks?

IMO, you should focus either on:

-Chameleon (Arishat and co. as friends, with vote push and Banishments)
-Madness Network (maybe getting Heart of the City and bleed retainers and profiting from Shalmath's special)

I really don't see how your deck will work...

Messages.Author: Borrelstein
Messages.Body:
To start off, 30 actions seems too much even for Shalmath, you are going to clog.

The deck has a lot of moving parts, and in this version it is not too dangerous to block Shalmath; maybe add 2 Decapitate to punish people for blocking. People WILL try to block Chameleon actions anyway.

Regarding the moving parts, relying on Clan Impersonation is tricky and not too flexible if you also need to be an anarch baron. If Shalmath changes to Malkavian, he changes sects as well hence the Baron title becomes inactive (if he already had it), so you loose additional actions and blood to become anarch again. For that purpose, a few anarch converts in the crypt may be handy to make it easier to switch back or to become anarch again, and you will be ready for Chameleon actions one turn earlier. You do not want to loose your window to play Chameleon!

I would also add an Enkil Kog just in case the Madness Network is removed, and extra ousting power.

Messages.Author: Klaital
Messages.Body: The main issue I see in this deck is kind of same as with form of corruption, only worse. Form of Corruption discourages your prey to go forward, this one discourages your prey from spending their pool to bring out new vampires, which combined with the really small pressure you are putting on their pool means that in most cases you will just end up screwing the game of whoever is sitting front of you before you get ousted.
